canonical_statement: Let T > 0 and let X = (X_t)_{t in [0,T]} be a real-valued stochastic process. If there are real constants alpha > 0, beta > 0, and C >= 0 such that E[|X_t - X_s|^alpha] <= C |t-s|^(1+beta) for all s,t in [0,T], then X has a modification Y such that, for every gamma with 0 < gamma < beta/alpha, almost every sample path t |-> Y_t is gamma-Holder continuous on [0,T].
domain_and_universes: Provisional Lean scope: a measurable probability space (Omega, F, P); T alpha beta C : Real; X : Set.Icc (0 : Real) T -> Omega -> Real; Prop in universe 0. Exact process, expectation, and Holder encodings remain statement-phase decisions.
quantifiers: for every measurable probability space (Omega, F, P)
for every real T > 0 and real-valued process X indexed by [0,T]
for every alpha > 0, beta > 0, and C >= 0 satisfying the increment moment bound
there exists a real-valued process Y indexed by [0,T]
for every gamma with 0 < gamma < beta / alpha
hypotheses: each X_t is measurable and the alpha moment of each increment is defined
for all s,t in [0,T], E[|X_t-X_s|^alpha] <= C |t-s|^(1+beta)
conclusion: There exists Y such that X_t = Y_t almost surely for every fixed t, and for every 0 < gamma < beta/alpha, almost every path t |-> Y_t obeys a finite gamma-Holder bound on [0,T].

coordinatewise almost-everywhere equality alone is not path continuity
assuming in advance that X has continuous paths does not satisfy the construction conclusion
